children: allows the San Diego-based semiconductor company to establish a "foothold in the important data center AI segment," according to RBC Capital Markets.

The agreement entails Amazon purchasing Qualcomm's server chip products, technology, systems and manufacturing services. In return, Qualcomm issued a warrant to Amazon, granting it the right to acquire up to 25M shares of Qualcomm common stock at an exercise price of $161.26 per share. The vesting is linked to purchase orders and payments up to a maximum of $60B. The first 3.75M shares vest immediately based on initial purchase commitments, with the remainder vesting in tranches as commercial milestones are met.
The deal prompted RBC to increase its price target on Qualcomm to $180 from $160 and maintain its Sector Perform rating.

"The overall revenue opportunity could potentially amount to ~$6B of incremental annual revenue over the next 10 years (assuming full vesting) vs. management's prior Data Center targets of ~$300M and ~$5B for FY26 and FY27, respectively," said RBC analyst Srini Pajjuri in an investor note. "Management expects to begin recognizing revenue from the agreement in the Dec-26Q as certain programs are already in production. Lack of upward revisions to FY26/27 targets suggests that the disclosure is largely a formalization (and possibly an extension) of prior agreement. Nevertheless, we are encouraged by the disclosure that AMZN is one of the two hyperscaler customers given the scale and custom silicon opportunity."

title: Qualcomm's deal with Amazon establishes 'foothold' in AI data center sector: RBC
